title: Strict completed tensor and coefficient-extension towers under clopen restriction
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a finite set, and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions whose images cover $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the small pro-etale sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived categories and cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible on $X$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_{E,n})_X$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $r_i$ for restriction, using the canonical coefficient identifications. Let $P\to M$ and $Q\to N$ be K-flat flat-term resolutions of arbitrary $M,N\in D(R)$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_X$ and $Q_n=Q\otimes_R(A_{E,n})_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The pure-tensor comparisons induce isomorphisms of strict towers of complexes of $R_i$-modules
$$r_i\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_n(P_n\otimes_{(A_{E,n})_X}Q_n)\bigr)_n\cong\bigl(\operatorname{Res}_{i,n}((r_iP)_n\otimes_{(A_{E,n})_{X_i}}(r_iQ)_n)\bigr)_n.$$
Their level maps send $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)$ to $(r_ip\otimes r_ia)\otimes(r_iq\otimes r_ib)$; they commute with the transitions induced by $\rho_n:A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$ in both factors and with all strict tower maps. Here $\operatorname{Res}_n$ and $\operatorname{Res}_{i,n}$ read the finite-level complexes through the completed coefficient projections. There are resulting natural isomorphisms in $D(R_i)$
$$r_i(M\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}^L_{\mathcal O_E}N)\cong r_iM\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}^L_{\mathcal O_E}r_iN$$
for the strict-Roos operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The coefficient object $R$, its section $1$, all finite quotient coefficient units, and their transitions restrict to the corresponding component objects and maps.

For every finite extension $E\subset L$ with chosen uniformizer $\varpi_L$, put $A_{L,m}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$, $R_L=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X}$ and $\rho^L_m=(\iota_m)_X\pi^E_m:R\to(A_{L,m})_X$ as in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. The complexes $P_{L,m}=P\otimes_R(A_{L,m})_X$, read as $R_L$-modules through $\pi^L_m$, have strict tower comparisons
$$r_i(\operatorname{Res}^L_mP_{L,m})_m\cong(\operatorname{Res}^L_{i,m}(r_iP\otimes_{R_i}(A_{L,m})_{X_i}))_m.$$
Their maps $p\otimes a\mapsto r_ip\otimes r_ia$ commute with every level unit $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and every transition $p\otimes a\mapsto p\otimes\bar a$, using the same coefficient inclusion $\iota_m$ and quotient projections. They yield natural isomorphisms in $D(R_L|_{X_i})$
$$r_i(M\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L)\cong(r_iM)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L,$$
including the specified level maps and transitions. These derived comparisons are those induced by the strict cone maps and are independent of the chosen resolutions; they assert no canonical cone construction in a bare triangulated category. No unramifiedness or completeness of $M,N$ is assumed. All assertions hold for empty components and the empty partition.

Tensor products of complexes here use the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Strict towers and their morphisms are inverse systems of complexes [def-weil-inverse-system]; scalar restriction has the meaning of [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.12(4), p. 22; Proposition 3.5.1(3) and Definition 3.5.2, p. 24. Agent finite-clopen strict tensor and integral scalar extension application, returned proof steps 8-9; explicit tower definitions def-pur-integral-derived-operations and def-weil-integral-scalar-extension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to the completed and finite coefficient rings. It identifies $r_iR$ with $R_i$ and $r_i(A_{E,n})_X$ with $(A_{E,n})_{X_i}$, preserving $1$, the projections $\pi_n$ and coefficient transitions. The final two equivalences of [lem-pur-clopen-total-tensor-kflat-detection], applied to each term and to the whole complex respectively, show that restriction preserves flat terms and K-flatness; by [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization] it preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes derived restriction. Thus $r_iP\to r_iM$ and $r_iQ\to r_iN$ are admissible resolutions with exactly the hypotheses required in the component operation definitions. The Lean proofs of exactness and resolving-class preservation use the proved ring-isomorphism tensor-transport theorem for the normalized completed coefficient isomorphism. Exactness uses its underlying equivalence; flatness and K-flatness use its flat_iff and kflat_iff clauses.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: For $a=\pi_n:R\to B_n=(A_{E,n})_X$, [lem-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-compositor] supplies the $B_{i,n}$-linear chain isomorphisms $\beta^P_n:r_i(P\otimes_R B_n)\cong r_iP\otimes_{R_i}B_{i,n}$ and $\beta^Q_n$, with the specified formula $p\otimes a\mapsto r_ip\otimes r_ia$. The coefficient projections were identified in step 1. The definition [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] leaves underlying sheaves and maps unchanged: both restricted $R_i$-actions are $u\cdot z=\pi_{i,n}(u)z$. Therefore these are also isomorphisms after the indicated scalar restrictions. Substituting $a=1$ shows directly that $\beta^P_n r_i(p\mapsto p\otimes1)$ is $r_ip\mapsto r_ip\otimes1$.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: Apply $b_{i,P_n,Q_n}$ of [lem-pur-clopen-total-tensor-kflat-detection] with coefficient ring $B_n$, then compose with $\beta^P_n\otimes\beta^Q_n$ from step 2. The cited statement identifies its map on each $(p,q)$ direct-sum summand with $a_{i,P_n^p,Q_n^q}$ and gives the differential $r_i(dx)\otimes r_iy+(-1)^p r_ix\otimes r_i(dy)$. Thus the composite is a chain isomorphism $c_n$ from the restricted level $\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{B_n}Q_n)$ to the stated component level for arbitrary unbounded $P_n,Q_n$; no K-flatness assumption on these finite-level complexes is needed for this application. On local sheafified pure tensors it sends $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)$ to $(r_ip\otimes r_ia)\otimes(r_iq\otimes r_ib)$. The node supplies naturality on all chain maps and the explicit signed symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$. Scalar restriction preserves this chain isomorphism by the action calculation of step 2 [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: The transition in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] takes $(p\otimes a)\otimes(q\otimes b)$ to $(p\otimes\rho_n(a))\otimes(q\otimes\rho_n(b))$. Either order around its square with $c_{n+1}$ and $c_n$ gives $(r_ip\otimes\rho_{i,n}(r_ia))\otimes(r_iq\otimes\rho_{i,n}(r_ib))$, since $r_i\rho_n=\rho_{i,n}$ by step 1. These equalities on pure tensors determine equal sheaf maps by the bilinear universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal], applied successively, and then determine maps out of each total direct sum. Thus $(c_n)_n$ is an isomorphism of strict towers. Naturality of the chain tensorator and the scalar comparisons gives the same squares for maps of $P,Q$. More generally it is natural for all strict tower maps: write the component level map as $c'_n r_i(f_n)c_n^{-1}$; its transition equation is the restriction of $f_nt_n=t'_nf_{n+1}$.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, use exactly the ring maps $\rho^L_m=(\iota_m)_X\pi^E_m$ in [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. On an object of the component site the restricted constant presheaf map is still $\iota_m$; functorial sheafification, from the unique factorization in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], in the constant-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] gives its component constant-sheaf map. The projection compatibility in step 1 therefore identifies $r_i\rho^L_m$ with $(\iota_m)_{X_i}\pi^E_{i,m}$. Apply [lem-pur-clopen-derived-scalar-compositor] to this map and $P$: its chain isomorphism $d_m$ sends $p\otimes a$ to $r_ip\otimes r_ia$. Applying the coefficient clause of [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to $L$ identifies $r_iR_L$ with $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,X_i}$ and $r_i(A_{L,m})_X$ with $(A_{L,m})_{X_i}$, preserving $1$, the projections $\pi^L_m$ and the transitions $(A_{L,m+1})_X\to(A_{L,m})_X$. Hence both $R_L|_{X_i}$-actions after scalar restriction are through $\pi^L_{i,m}$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Both paths in the unit square give $r_ip\otimes1$; both paths in the transition square give $r_ip\otimes\overline{r_ia}$, because restriction preserves the quotient maps. The same bilinear universal property as step 4 proves equality of the maps. These $d_m$ therefore give the required natural strict tower isomorphism, including units, for ramified as well as unramified extensions.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: For the exact additive restriction functor, prove preservation of countable products by composing with the faithful module-to-presheaf forgetful functor, which reflects limits. The clopen site restriction commutes with the corresponding presheaf product and the completed coefficient scalar transport is an equivalence. Apply the additive Roos comparison of [lem-pur-roos-additive-comparison], using the strict shifted-cone coordinate formulas of [lem-pur-injective-tower-roos-shifts]. Its first and second projections give exactly RoosNormalized for the identity tower comparison. Thus the comparison is a natural isomorphism before localization, including unbounded towers.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: Localize step 6. The specified representative comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] and [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] identify both sides with the respective derived operation functors on flat-term K-flat inputs. Step 1 gives the admissible component resolutions. To justify naturality beyond such inputs, apply [lem-sc-nattrans-from-resolving-class] on the homotopy category, with $W$ the quasi-isomorphisms, $P$ the flat-term K-flat objects, and $A,B$ the two already defined derived functors precomposed with localization. Here $W$ admits right fractions by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], every object receives a $W$-map from $P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and $A$ inverts $W$. The chain naturality of steps 2-6 gives the hypothesis on maps between $P$-objects. For tensor apply this first in one variable, then the other; the naturality equations in the second variable persist after the first extension because they hold on representatives and can be conjugated by the invertible images of their resolution maps. The inverse chain comparisons extend too; these conjugation equations show their two composites are identities. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) descends these natural isomorphisms from homotopy categories to derived categories, in each variable. The same equations force compatibility with any resolution computation comparison. Thus the derived comparisons are natural and independent of resolutions, retaining the coefficient and unit maps already calculated. This construction localizes strict cone maps only.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Proposition 3.5.1(3), Definition 3.5.2; agent strict-clopen calculation using the specified operation models.

proof.text: Empty components have zero module, complex and derived categories by [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] and [lem-pur-clopen-unbounded-derived-localization]. Every displayed map there is the unique map and is an isomorphism. If $I$ is empty, the covering hypothesis forces $X=\varnothing$, so the same applies globally. No preceding step assumes boundedness or completeness of $M,N$; the only resolution hypotheses used are K-flatness, flat terms and a quasi-isomorphism, and the coefficient maps of step 5 require no unramifiedness.
